DBB. Mixed CRT & Ramified Locality 
  Through‑line  ·  The Conductor Branch  DAY routed ramified and multi‑factor SELECT; DBC made it an end‑to‑end primitive; DBA‑odd proved the local law \(c(p^a)=a+1\). DBB stress‑tests the seam where the architecture could be accused of cherry‑picking: conductors that are both CRT‑factorised and ramified at once.  
  L ocality used to mean one coordinate. For \(L=15=3\cdot5\) a term was \(3\)‑local, \(5\)‑local, or cross‑factor. DBB upgrades locality to two coordinates:  which  CRT factor, and  which  \(p\)‑adic depth inside that factor. A term can be local to the \(3^2\) component yet deep in its \(3\)‑adic filtration; another local to \(5^2\); another genuinely coupling \(3^2\) and \(5\). The question is whether conductor‑local SELECT stays local when locality carries both structures at once, or whether the earlier wins quietly depended on friendly squarefree examples. The arithmetic answer is clean: the Weil commutant factorises under the Chinese Remainder Theorem, so the proved odd law multiplies, \(c(L)=\prod_i(a_i+1)\) — verified directly on the small mixed conductors \(45,75,63,99\) (each \(c=6=3\cdot2\)) by the DBA congruence‑kernel method, hence \(c(225)=3\cdot3=9\), \(c(135)=4\cdot2=8\), \(c(175)=3\cdot2=6\), \(c(315)=3\cdot2\cdot2=12\). The compiler answer is the load‑bearing one: across the odd‑only stress set \(225=3^2\!\cdot5^2\), \(135=3^3\!\cdot5\), \(175=5^2\!\cdot7\), \(315=3^2\!\cdot5\cdot7\), every depth‑stratum and parity term routes to a  local  class — \(\mathcal K_X^{\mathrm{local}}\), \(\mathcal M_X^{\mathrm{ramified}}\), or \(\mathcal M_X^{\mathrm{local}}\) — and the number of global seams equals the number of genuine cross‑factor couplings, never more. Ramification does not buy a global seam. A \(p^2\)‑deep operator inside \(3^2\) pays a projector or a ramified‑local measurement; it pays a global entangler only when it truly couples distinct CRT factors.

  Figure 162.  Mixed CRT + ramified locality. Each odd mixed conductor factorises into CRT factors, each carrying its own \(p\)‑adic depth; the Weil commutant multiplies as \(c(L)=\prod_i(a_i+1)\) (DBA‑odd per factor, CRT‑verified on \(45,75,63,99\)). Routed through DAY’s six‑way dispatch, every depth and parity term lands in a local class and the global‑seam count equals the number of genuine cross‑factor couplings (\(1\) for \(225\), \(2\) for \(315\)) — ramification never escalates to global. Over the qubitization query count the saved all‑channel exposure compounds. Dyadic mixed towers \(2^a p^b\) are excluded until DBA‑dyadic defines the correct object. Computed from  tqc.mixed_ramified . 
 
  DBB · Mixed Locality Compounds Without Dyadic Assumptions   Verified   For odd conductors \(L=\prod_i p_i^{a_i}\), conductor‑local SELECT remains local under two‑coordinate locality. The Weil commutant factorises, \(c(L)=\prod_i(a_i+1)\) (the proved odd law \(c(p^a)=a+1\) times CRT multiplicativity, verified on \(45,75,63,99\)); and across the odd‑only stress set \(225,135,175,315\) the six‑way DAY dispatch routes every depth and parity term to a local class, with the number of global seams equal to the number of genuine cross‑factor couplings — a prime‑power factor never escalates to a global seam merely for being ramified. Over the qubitization query count the saved all‑channel exposure compounds. Hence mixed CRT + ramified locality compounds conductor‑local savings without importing dyadic assumptions; dyadic mixed towers are excluded until DBA‑dyadic exists.  
 Verified (exact arithmetic, backend‑free): CRT multiplicativity \(c(L)=\prod_i(a_i+1)\) of the Weil commutant on \(45,75,63,99\) via the DBA congruence‑kernel method; the six‑way dispatch on \(225,135,175,315\) read from the operators; the invariant that the number of global seams equals the number of genuine cross‑factor couplings, so ramified and depth terms never escalate to global; the per‑query and end‑to‑end all‑channel exposure deltas under the DAX branch tensor through a DAW profile. Predicted: \(c(L)\) for the large targets \(225,135,175,315\) is the proved odd law \(c(p^a)=a+1\) multiplied across CRT factors. Warrant: \(\texttt{mixed\_ramified}\) ( 4410a2a74b7d9fbd ), verdict  true ; shipped inside the DBV four‑layer harness (unit, integration, e2e, release). BOUNDARY: an exposure/transaction‑count advantage over a structure‑blind globalising baseline, not a claim of beating an optimised Pauli‑LCU on a device. OPEN/EXCLUDED: \(2^a p^b\) dyadic mixed towers await DBA‑dyadic (the cyclic Weil pair gives the wrong dyadic sequence \(1,3,8,19,\dots\)); deeper towers \(a\ge4\) in the benchmark; the DAM distance‑suppressed cost‑model tie‑in. Scope: odd mixed conductors only.
